q: briatico the deepest line in this archive, and the one that does not carry the surname. a small comune on the tyrrhenian coast of briatico - the mazza archive skip to the content part i · three towns on a strait · i.6 ← prev next : i.7 scilla → contents vibo valentia, calabria briatico the deepest line in this archive, and the one that does not carry the surname. a small comune on the tyrrhenian coast of calabria that sent its people to three different continents. 14 september 2026 · the keystone act 1 of 1849, and the family turns out not to be from briatico on 14 june 1849 , before antonino bajoni, sindaco of briatico, domenico prostamo married giovanna ventrice . the act runs to nine lines and every one of them was new. he is di anni trentasei - thirty-six, so born about 1813 , where the family tree says 1820. he is a marinaro . and he is nato in pizzo : not briatico, not potenzoni, but a town eleven kilometres up the coast. he is figlio di antonino , di professione marinaro, domiciliato defunto, e di maria fragala , domiciliata al pizzo . that single clause does two things. it documents the fourth generation , which this archive has carried as untested - family tree only, no source - since it began; and the tree's name for him, antonino, turns out to be exactly right. it also produces maria fragala , who was not in the tree at all: a widow still living at pizzo while her son had moved along the coast. the bride is twenty-one and born at briatico, figlia di giuseppe , di professione bracciale, domiciliato defunto, e caterina cichello , who came to the wedding and gave her consent in person. two more names, both new. and it explains the silence. three complete years of briatico births - 1818, 1819, 1820 - hold no prostamo of any given name. thirteen years of briatico marriages hold none either. the reason is not that the register is thin. the prostamo were not there yet. this act is the family's first appearance in the town, and the work now moves to pizzo , whose registers this archive has never opened. one more line is worth keeping. the groom produced la fede di morte del padre, e dell' avo paterno - his grandfather's death certificate. so the third generation was dead by 1849 and his death act exists. the tree, independently, puts pasquale prostamo's death at pizzo on 4 january 1829. two things agreeing is not a source, and the generation stays marked untested until that act is opened - but they agree, and they agree about pizzo. briatico, stato civile della restaurazione, matrimoni 1849, atto 1 - archivio di stato di catanzaro (antenati an_ua87663 , image 2). 14 september 2026 · the marriage bundle antonino prostamo died in the cholera, and the bundle proves the line every i

1913 read in full, all 58 marriages, and it is not there). death: scilla 1975, act 30 what it settles the marriage would give both spouses' ages, trades and parents, and giovanni polistena's own parents, where this archive has only the 1908 new orleans manifest's statement. the death act would give her date and place of birth and name her parents a second time. her father michele donato's own birthplace has since been settled from the free registers (scilla, 3 october 1855), so that is no longer the reason to ask. what to ask for an estratto per riassunto of each act, for genealogical research. this is normally free. a copia integrale can require a stated legal interest, so ask for the summary. send it to the ufficio di stato civile by pec or ordinary email; and four of those plots are consecutive. nudgee cemetery, beside holy cross church at banyo, has been the catholic burying ground of northern brisbane since the 1860s. it is run by the archdiocese, not the city council, which is why it does not appear in the brisbane city council grave search and why the family tree recorded the cemetery but never a plot. the archdiocese keeps its own register, and it was read on 10 september 2026 . it supplies a plot, a register number, a date of birth, a date of death and a date of interment for 19 people in this archive - and it corrects the family tree in 6 places. the finding four plots in a row michael rocco mazza's four grandparents were born in three towns - piedimonte etneo on etna, briatico on the tyrrhenian coast, and scilla on the strait - about 130 kilometres apart, in families that had never met. they arrived in australia between 1949 and 1953 on four different sailings. they are buried in four consecutive plots . v-1026 sebastiano mazza 22 october 1920 - 2 april 2002 v-1027 domenica prostamo - entered in the register as domenica mazza 3 may 1928 - 29 january 2010 v-1028 angela polistena - entered in the register as angelina arena 22 january 1925 - 18 september 2018 v-1029 rocco arena 12 october 1924 - 29 october 1999 two married couples, side by side, in the order they died: rocco arena in 1999, sebastiano mazza in 2002, domenica prostamo in 2010, angela polistena in 2018. nineteen years between the first burial and the last, and the plots were held. where the register beats the tree 6 corrections a burial register is a contemporary administrative record made by the people who did the burying. a family tree is a recollection typed in later. where they disagree, this archive believes the register - s: The town on the north-east flank of Etna that gave this family its surname — and, of the four quarters, the one the arch
q: piedimonte etneo the town on the north-east flank of etna that gave this family its surname - and, of the four quarters, the one the arch piedimonte etneo - the mazza archive skip to the content part i · three towns on a strait · i.2 ← prev next : i.3 giarre → contents catania, sicily piedimonte etneo the town on the north-east flank of etna that gave this family its surname - and, of the four quarters, the one the archive knows least about. 50 people placed at piedimonte etneo 1809 the earliest mazza birth with a date 6 mazza still joined to nothing the town piedimonte etneo means the foot of the mountain, and it is exactly that: a comune of the province of catania standing on the north-eastern slope of etna , above fiumefreddo and the alcantara valley, looking out at the ionian sea. the neighbouring towns in this archive - mascali , giarre , linguaglossa 's side of the mountain - are all within a few kilometres. living on etna is a recurring administrative fact, not a metaphor. in 1928 the eruption that destroyed the town of mascali - the only town etna has swallowed whole in modern times - happened eight years after sebastiano mazza was born here, and the archive records mascali as a birthplace for people in this family. the sicilian quarter is four towns, not one piedimonte etneo gave the family its surname. it did not give it everybody. for most of this archive's life the sicilian side was a single town, and the family tree still says so: it puts maria nicotra at piedimonte etneo, where her husband was born. four consecutive documents, read in september 2026, take her and her father somewhere else - and the towns are all within eight kilometres of each other, down the same coast road. piedimonte etneo - the mazza , back to mariano mazza and maria catalano, both alive and working there in april 1871. also where venera cassaniti was born in 1848, and where she and giovanni nicotra married on 7 october 1872. mascali - where giovanni nicotra was living in 1872, and where maria nicotra was born on 8 december 1875 , at half past nine in the evening, in contrada sopra pietrafitta . her birth act was found here after fourteen consecutive piedimonte birth indexes had been read without her, because a wife went to her husband's comune and the children were registered there. giarre - where the 1872 publication certificate says giovanni nicotra himself was nato . eleven giarre birth years, 1838 to 1848, have been read end to end, main runs and appendices, and they do not hold him. for a day this archive let that stand for the town and wrote that giarre's only nicotra was a dottor don . then its first year was opened: 1820 holds two untitled nicotra households , and one of the fathers is a rosario.

eleven giarre birth years, read end to end in both the main run and the appendix, do not hold him . mascali , where he was living in 1872, does not hold him either - nine years read there. riposto is the lower town, the port below giarre, and it has registered separately since 1821 - through the whole window in which he was born. a man of the lower town could say giarre and be entered here. that is a reading from general history and not from any document , and it is written down as such. what makes it more than a guess is what the registers hold. giarre's only nicotra across eleven years is a dottor don with a donna wife. mascali's across nine is an alfio. riposto has three ordinary nicotra households - the sort of family a bracciante belongs to. and in september 2026 the reading stopped being an inference. riposto's marriage tavola for 1844 records nicotra salvadore, patria giarre , marrying a riposto woman - and his two children then appear in riposto's own birth tavole, in 1845 and 1847. a nicotra who says giarre and is registered here is no longer a theory about how people moved; it is a man with an act number. the nicotra of riposto father mother seen the children giuseppe nicotra angela autieri 1847, 1848 nicotra rosa in november 1847 and nicotra leonardo on 26 december 1848 salvadore nicotra maria barbagallo 1844, 1845, 1847 married maria barbagallo at riposto in july 1844 (matrimoni atto 39), and his own patria there is giarre. children alfio on 9 may 1845 and rosa on 15 november 1847 francesco nicotra - 1838 nicotra maria, entry 170; q: testing the 1697 the archive's largest claim is eleven generations to franco antonino prostamo, born at briatico about 1697. four of thos testing the 1697 - the mazza archive skip to the content part vi · how we know, and what is missing · vi.6 ← prev next : vi.7 what has been read → contents the prostamo line, audited testing the 1697 the archive's largest claim is eleven generations to franco antonino prostamo, born at briatico about 1697. four of those generations rest on nothing at all, and they are not testable online. this archive has said since the day it opened that its deepest line is the prostamo of briatico - nine generations to 1697 , reached through a grandmother, and deeper than the surname it is named for. on 10 september 2026 the same family tree was found to be six years out on salvatore mazza's birth, six years out on orazio's, four on alfonso prostamo's, and wrong about the town where salvatore died. a tree with that error rate is not a source, and the 1697 rests on it entirely. so it was audited. generation by generation gen who born standing what supports it 1 franco antonino prostamo 1697 untested family tree only. no source. pre-dates civil registration (1809) and familysearch's briatico coverage (1880-1910). not testable online. 2 antonino prostamo 1726 untested family tree only. no source. 3 pasquale prostamo c. 1753, at pizzo documented his death act, and the proof of the descent. pizzo, morti 1829, atto 7: pasquale prostamo, marinaro, vedovo di caterina majo, born at pizzo, of the castello quarter, died there on 13 january 1829. the descent is no longer an assertion: a certified extract of this very act was filed in domenico prostamo's marriage papers at briatico in june 1849 as the groom's «fede di morte dell'avo paterno» - so pasquale was domenico's paternal grandfather, which is to say antonino's father. two documents disagree about his age: the original register says settantacinque (75, born c. 1753); the chancery's own certified copy of 1849 says sessantacinque (65, born c. 1763). this archive carries the original's figure. his own parents' lines in the act are blank, and he married before civil registration began in 1809, so the generation above him is probably not reachable online at all. 4 antonino prostamo c. 1781, at pizzo documented named in three documents and dead in a fourth. he declares his son's birth at pizzo on 2 april 1814, «antonino prostamo di anni trentadue, di professione marinaro, domiciliato alle moli», with his «legittima moglie maria fragala di anni ventisette». he is «il fu antonino» in the pizzo marriage banns of april 1849 and in his son's briatico marriage act of 14 june 1849. and he died in the cholera: pizzo's separate register of

q: the crossings this family emigrated twice, in two waves half a century apart, to opposite sides of the world. the first went to americ the crossings - the mazza archive skip to the content part iii · the crossings, and brisbane · iii.1 ← prev next : iii.2 brisbane → contents eighteen recorded arrivals and departures the crossings this family emigrated twice, in two waves half a century apart, to opposite sides of the world. the first went to america. the second went to australia. both left from the same three towns. the manifests , read properly - 14 september 2026 four crossings, four ships, and a column nobody had read this site has carried rocco arena 's four atlantic crossings as a list with one ship named and one year marked probable . all four are indexed, with the vessel, the port and a birth year - 1861 on every one . four clerks over twenty-one years, agreeing with a birth act of 20 december 1861 that none of them had seen. 1892 elysia , out of naples - aged 31 his first 1894 suevia , out of naples - aged 33 no longer "probable" 1900 trave , out of genoa - aged 39 , us citizen , residence scilla naturalised already 1913 san guglielmo , out of messina - aged 52 , us citizen the last the 1900 line says something the archive did not know: in march 1900 he was already an american citizen and living at scilla . three months later the census finds him in manhattan with a wife and two children. he was going back and forth with a passport, not emigrating. the column nobody had read a passenger manifest has two relation fields - who you left behind at the departure port, and who you were going to at the arrival port. this archive had never used them. the 1913 line reads: departure port relation (wife): corta generosa arrival port relation (nephew): antonio arena so generosa costa - her surname mangled to corta - stayed at messina, and rocco sailed to a nephew in new york. a nephew of that name would be a son of giovanni or giuseppe arena , and the family tree has no such person. recorded as a lead : rocco's own son antonio was born in manhattan in 1896 and would have been seventeen, and a clerk could have written nephew for son . reading the neighbours is the technique. it is also what exposed the clementina error below: the line above hers named a father and a residence four hundred kilometres from this family. a manifest line on its own is a name; a manifest line with its neighbours is a household. re-read - the mazza archive the mazza archive skip to the content front matter · f.1 next : f.2 about → contents a family history, kept honestly three towns, one strait, and a suburb of brisbane. piedimonte etneo · briatico · scilla · new york · buenos aires · brisbane - a family assembled from three corners of the italian south, and the ships that carried it. this is an archive of the mazza of brisbane - and of the three southern italian towns they came out of, none of which had heard of the other two. it is not a pedigree: of the 790 people recorded here, all but a handful never continued the line. only 134 of them have a death recorded anywhere - which is a measure of how much of this tree is still undated rather than of who is still alive. this archive opened with the mazza name reaching back four generations and stopping at a man with no dates at all. one day in the sicilian registers took it to seven generations and mariano mazza and maria catalano , and joined a hundred and ten cousins to the line - every step a document. the same day cost the archive its other headline. the calabrian prostamo were said to run nine generations to 1697 . audited, they are documented to a sailor dead before 1886 , and asserted for four generations above him . it is a public archive with one rule: a living person (80 or younger, with no death recorded) is named with their relationships and their town and country, and nothing more . and a second rule, which is harder: every claim says how well it is known . documented inferred family lore the four quarters four families out of three towns about 130 kilometres apart - mazza, prostamo, arena, polistena - and where each of them met the others. compare them → a claim, tested the prostamo were said to reach 1697. the audit shows what is documented, what is asserted, and by a tree already wrong by six years elsewhere. the audit → four plots in a row all four of michael rocco mazza's grandparents lie in consecutive plots v-1026 to v-1029, having arrived on four different sailings. the register → where this family can actually be put calabrian towns on one side of the strait, four sicilian comuni within ten kilometres on the other, and a brisbane parish where the quarters met. every dot is a place this archive can put a named person in, and its size is how many stand there. the biggest are labelled; the colours are this archive's own regions. the coast and the borders under them are real - natural earth, clipped to this frame - so a dot can be read as somewhere rather than as a position in an empty box. giarre piedimonte etneo brisbane riposto new york

that he fathered salvatore - while the calabrian prostamo ran nine generations to 1697. that is no longer true. on 10 september 2026 the sicilian registers gave up salvatore's act of birth, and with it his father's age, his father's street, and his father's father. the act that did it piedimonte etneo, nati 1873, atto 3 …e comparso rosario mazza di mariano , di anni ventotto , bracciante, qui domiciliato, il quale mi ha presentato un bambino di sesso maschile che dichiara essergli nato il giorno cinque corrente gennaro alle ore sette antemeridiane, dalla di lui moglie leonarda bonanno di gaetano , seco lui domiciliata nella casa di sua abitazione sita in questo comune contrada terremorte , al quale figlio dichiara di dare il nome di salvadore . three things in one sentence. salvatore mazza was born on 5 january 1873 - q: the name what the surnames in this archive mean, roughly how common they are, and - the useful part - how much that tells you abo the name - the mazza archive skip to the content part i · three towns on a strait · i.8 ← prev next : ii four grandparents, four families → contents mazza, and the nine names around it the name what the surnames in this archive mean, roughly how common they are, and - the useful part - how much that tells you about whether two people who share one are related. mazza mazza is the italian for a club, a mace or a mallet, from the latin mattea . as a surname it was coined in all the usual ways at once: as a nickname for a strong or a violent man, as a trade name for someone who worked with a mallet or a maul, and - most often - from the medieval personal name mazzo , itself a short form of names like giacomazzo and tommazzo. it is one of the most widespread surnames in italy, found from lombardy to sicily, and it was coined independently many times over . there is no founding mazza family. two mazza households in the same sicilian town are much more likely to be related than two mazza in different provinces - but "much more likely" is a probability, and this archive does not publish probabilities as descents. that is precisely the situation at piedimonte etneo , where 121 mazza sit in seven groups that no record joins. the others name here where it belongs what it is prostamo 79 briatico, vibo valentia rare, and concentrated. almost the whole italian distribution sits in a few calabrian comuni around vibo valentia. a rare surname in one small place is the best gift a genealogist gets: two prostamo of briatico almost certainly are related. polistena 40 scilla, reggio calabria a toponymic - from the town of polistena in the province of reggio calabria. it marks a family that moved from there, and was named for having done so. arena 65 scilla, reggio calabria very common across calabria and sicily; q: the pieces the export arrived as fourteen separate pieces. reading the sicilian registers joined the largest two, and it is ten now the pieces - the mazza archive skip to the content part iv · how the lines join · iv.4 ← prev next : v everyone, and everything in order → contents the different lines, joined and unjoined the pieces the export arrived as fourteen separate pieces. reading the sicilian registers joined the largest two, and it is ten now - but the point of the page is unchanged: a file that draws as one tree is not necessarily one family. open a gedcom in any family-tree program and it draws every person on one canvas. that canvas is a rendering choice , not a finding. underneath, the file is a graph - and this one falls into 10 disconnected pieces with no edge of any kind between them. naming the pieces is not pedantry. the largest holds 560 people ; q: the queensland register the registry's historical index is free, it is authoritative, and - the part that matters - it can be searched by a fath the queensland register - the mazza archive skip to the content part vi · how we know, and what is missing · vi.4 ← prev next : vi.5 the audit → contents read 10 september 2026 the queensland register the registry's historical index is free, it is authoritative, and - the part that matters - it can be searched by a father's or a mother's name. one search returned three of sebastiano mazza's siblings. the queensland registry of births, deaths and marriages publishes a searchable historical index: deaths to 1996, marriages to 1951, births to 1926 . every death and birth entry carries the names of both parents , and the search box will take a parent's name as the query. that turns it from a lookup into a reconstruction tool . searching "salvatore mazza" in the father field returns the deaths of his children - and each of those names their mother, which is how a family asserted by the tree became a family on the record. the finding michele mazza was sebastiano's brother michele mazza landed at brisbane on the palermo on 21 april 1925 , aged about sixteen, and died the following year. the family tree asserted he was kin and produced nothing to show it. the archive has carried the question since the day it was built: was he the reason they chose queensland? the registry's index answers it: michali mazza · death registration 14 november 1926 · 1926/c/3983 · father salvatori mazza · mother maria lecota . lecota is the index's rendering of nicotra - and the same search returns rosario mazza, born 1899 , whose parents are given in full as salvatore mazza and maria concetta nicotra . the same couple, spelled properly. so michele mazza was a son of salvatore mazza and maria nicotra , and therefore sebastiano mazza 's elder brother . he came out first, alone, at sixteen. he was dead within nineteen months. twenty-four years later his family followed him to the port he had landed at. the archive should say what it still cannot: whether anyone was waiting for sebastiano in 1949, and whether the family knew where the boy was buried. the index gives a date and a registration number, not a grave. c in the registration means a country event - he did not die in brisbane. four deaths, and what each one proves date name registration father mother 14 november 1926 michali mazza 1926/c/3983 salvatori mazza maria lecota 19 march 1986 rosario mazza (b. 1899) 1986/2455 salvatore mazza maria concetta nicotra 24 september 1963 maria nicotra mazza 1963/b/61348 john nicotra venera cassaneti 3 august 1968 mary rosa mazza 1968/b/936 sebastiano mazza domenica postamo 24 june 1928 helen m

q: the sicilian registers nine annual indexes and six acts, hunting one man. he is still missing - and in looking for him the archive found rosari the sicilian registers - the mazza archive skip to the content part vi · how we know, and what is missing · vi.3 ← prev next : vi.4 the queensland register → contents read 10 september 2026 the sicilian registers nine annual indexes and six acts, hunting one man. he is still missing - and in looking for him the archive found rosario, and a generation above him nobody knew was there. the family tree says salvatore mazza was born at piedimonte etneo in 1879 , son of a rosario mazza about whom exactly one thing was known: that he existed. finding salvatore's act of birth was supposed to name rosario and settle everything. salvatore is not in the register - not in 1875 , 1876 , 1877 , 1878 , 1879, 1880 , 1881 or 1882 at piedimonte etneo, nor at mascali or giarre in 1879. but the five mazza births that are there, and two marriage acts , have between them built three documented households , proved two of the men brothers , and reached a generation the family tree does not contain at all . the finding innocenzio mazza and domenica cavallaro a birth act names a father. a marriage act names both fathers and both mothers - which is why two marriages were worth more than five births. two of them, two years apart, name the same couple: 1874, atto 26 antonino mazza , di anni trentuno , bracciante, qui nato, figlio d'innocenzio , bracciante, e di domenica cavallaro , industriosa - marries rosa raiti , 20, daughter of giuseppe raiti and agata pennisi. 19 july 1874 1876, atto 5 mazza salvatore , di anni trentaquattro , bracciante, nato in piedimonte etneo, figlio di senzio e di cavallaro domenica - marries concetta sciacca , 19, daughter of the late antonino sciacca and rosaria greco. 16 january 1876 salvatore and antonino are brothers - born about 1841 and 1843, both braccianti of piedimonte etneo, both sons of domenica cavallaro . two independent acts, two years apart, naming the same mother. innocenzio mazza and domenica cavallaro are the earliest mazza this archive can name from a document - a couple of the 1810s or 1820s - and nothing in michael mazza's family tree reaches them. atto 26 of 1874 spells the father's name in full: innocenzio . atto 5 of 1876 contracts it to «senzio» - the same man, and the reading this archive got wrong first time. a correction, in the open this page said «venerio» for six hours, and it was wrong reading act 5 alone, this archive rendered the father's name as venerio -
